title: Cold rebuild: A typed cache
summary: Rebuild A typed cache from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **A typed cache** in *Generics*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Generics are erased too. What does this print?
code: function wrap<T>(value: T): { value: T; kind: string } {
steps.explain: There is no `typeof T` at run time: the type parameter is gone. `typeof` looks at the actual value, and arrays are `"object"`. (C# generics keep their types at run time; TypeScript's do not.)
